claims.claim: Nemotron-4 15B, a 15B-parameter multilingual LLM trained on 8 trillion text tokens
claims.quote: We introduce Nemotron-4 15B, a 15-billion-parameter large multilingual language model trained on 8 trillion text tokens.

claims.claim: Outperforms all similarly-sized open models on 4 of 7 evaluation areas and is competitive on the rest
claims.quote: it outperforms all existing similarly-sized open models on 4 out of 7 downstream evaluation areas and achieves competitive performance to the leading open models in the remaining ones

claims.claim: Best multilingual capabilities among similarly-sized models, attributed to significant multilingual training data
claims.quote: As Nemotron-4 15B was trained on significant amount of multilingual data, it is currently the state-of-the-art general purpose model in its size class on all multilingual benchmarks.

claims.claim: Designed to be the best general-purpose LLM that fits on a single A100 or H100 GPU
claims.quote: was developed to be the best general-purpose large language model (LLM) that can fit on a single NVIDIA A100 or H100 GPU

claims.claim: Better average accuracy across programming languages than Starcoder and Mistral 7B, especially on low-resource languages
claims.quote: we find that Nemotron-4 15B achieves better average accuracy, and in particular on low-resource programming languages, than Starcoder (Li et al., 2023), a code-specific model, and Mistral 7B.

rerun.quote: Results for Mistral are from our runs of Mistral in the same setting as Nemotron-4.

scores_copied.quote: we compare against a number of external decoder-only transformer language models and unless otherwise stated we use the numbers published in the reports of the corresponding models

data_disclosure.quote: the data blend is split into three different types of data: English natural language data (70%), multilingual natural language data (15%), and source-code data (15%).

tokens_disclosed.quote: We train Nemotron-4 15B on a pre-training dataset consisting of 8 trillion tokens.

compute_disclosed.quote: Training was completed in approximately 13 calendar days.

coding.note: There are no ARCH or TRAIN claims in the abstract or introduction, so no ablations are coded. The architecture uses standard components: RoPE, GQA and squared ReLU. Continued training is described on p.5 but is not presented as a contribution, and no ablation is shown for it. rerun is MIXED: the authors ran Mistral themselves for Tables 6 and 9, but most other scores are copied from published reports. scores_copied is coded YES even though a few Mistral runs were the authors' own, because most scores are copied; MIXED would also be defensible. Compute: 384 DGX H100 nodes (3,072 H100 GPUs) for about 13 days. Data disclosure is PARTIAL: the paper gives the high-level 70/15/15 split and language distributions only as figures.
